name: Cervical Radiculopathy
description: 4-phase program: Decompression, neural mobilization, strengthening, functional integration
pain_rule: Max. 4/10 local neck pain. With peripheralization (symptoms spreading toward arm/hand), stop immediately and adjust phase.
evidence_base: Thoomes et al. (2022): Exercise therapy for cervical radiculopathy
Nee & Butler (2006): Neural mobilization and neurodynamics
Kuijper et al. (2009): Cervical collar or physiotherapy
progression_criteria: Phase 1 to 2: 7 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 4/10, no peripheralization
Phase 2 to 3: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 4/10, no peripheralization in last 5 sessions
Phase 3 to 4: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, avg. pain ≤ 4/10, min. 1 centralization in last 5 sessions

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Acute Decompression**

Your nerve root is irritated. In this phase, we decompress the nerve and begin with gentle mobilization. Pay close attention to your arm symptoms.

**Goal:** Nerve decompression and symptom centralization.

**Strategy:**
- Cervical retraction (Chin Tuck) as nerve decompression
- Self-traction to create space for the nerve root
- Scapula setting for postural correction
- Avoid peripheralization — stop immediately if arm symptoms worsen

**Scientific basis:** McKenzie-based retraction is the most effective initial intervention for cervical radiculopathy (Clare et al., 2005). Centralization of symptoms is a positive prognostic factor.
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Neural Mobilization**

The nerve is gently mobilized. Nerve sliders are the foundation — they move the nerve without tensioning it.

**Goal:** Improved nerve mobility and neuromuscular control.

**Strategy:**
- Nerve Slider (nerve gliding) — gentle mobilization without tension
- CCF base training for deep musculature
- Thoracic extension for T-spine mobilization
- Daily symptom monitoring: centralization vs. peripheralization

**Scientific basis:** Neural mobilization (nerve sliders) improves nerve conductivity and reduces mechanical sensitivity (Nee & Butler, 2006). Slider techniques are safer than tensioners in the early phase.
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Strengthening With Nerve Progression**

Now we combine strengthening with progressive nerve loading. Nerve tensioners are added — controlled tension on the nerve.

**Goal:** Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening and nerve stress tolerance.

**Strategy:**
- Isometric neck exercises (flexion/extension)
- Progressive nerve tensioners (controlled nerve tension)
- Dynamic training (resistance band rows)
- Build nerve stress tolerance gradually

**Scientific basis:** Progressive nerve loading (tensioners) after an initial slider phase shows better outcomes than strengthening alone (Thoomes et al., 2022). The combination of strength and neural mobilization is the current gold standard.
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Functional Integration**

Your nerve tolerates loading. Now we test full everyday loading — carrying, overhead work, sport.

**Goal:** Full resilience with nerve stress tolerance and return to activity.

**Strategy:**
- Farmer Walk under load — posture and nerve stress tolerance
- Overhead Press for full shoulder chain loading
- Push-Up Plus for functional integration
- Sport-specific load tests with symptom monitoring

**Scientific basis:** Functional integration under load is the final step to full return. Habituation of the nerve to loading stimuli (graded exposure) significantly reduces recurrence rate (Kuijper et al., 2009).

exercises.name: Cervical Retraction (Decompression)
exercises.description: Gentle chin tuck focusing on nerve decompression. Stop immediately if peripheralizing symptoms occur.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Self-Traction
exercises.description: Seated: place hands under the back of the head, gently pull upward. Decompresses nerve roots.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Scapula Setting
exercises.description: Gently set the shoulder blades back and down and hold. Postural correction without loading.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Nerve Slider (Nerve Gliding)
exercises.description: Extend arm to the side, flex the wrist while tilting head to the same side. Gentle nerve gliding without tension.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Cranio-Cervical Flexion (Basic)
exercises.description: Supine, gently tuck the chin. Activate deep neck flexors without provoking arm symptoms.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension
exercises.description: Over a foam roller: T-spine extension. Improves posture and deloads the cervical spine.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Exercise (Flexion/Extension)
exercises.description: Hand resistance against the forehead (flexion) and back of head (extension). No arm pain allowed.
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Nerve Tensioner (Progressive)
exercises.description: Arm extended, wrist and head move simultaneously in opposite directions. Controlled nerve loading.
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Resistance Band Rows
exercises.description: Resistance band anchored in front, pull elbows back. Scapula stability under load.
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Farmer Walk
exercises.description: Carry heavy dumbbells. Full postural control under load, test nerve stress tolerance.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description: Shoulder press with dumbbells. Full shoulder chain under overhead load.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity

exercises.name: Push-Up Plus
exercises.description: Push-up with protraction at the top. Sport-/work-specific loading tolerance.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity

exercises.name: Supine Retraction (Maximum Gentle)
exercises.description: In supine: minimal chin tuck, pillow supports the neck. Focus on nerve decompression with zero effort.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Mini Nerve Slider
exercises.description: Seated: only flex/extend the wrist, head stays still. Minimal nerve gliding movement.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Isometrics Flexion Only (Gentle)
exercises.description: Only flexion against light hand resistance. No extension pressure. Monitor arm symptoms.
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Light Farmer Walk
exercises.description: Light weights (2–4 kg), short distances. Gently test nerve stress tolerance. Stop if arm symptoms arise.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity

exercises.name: Active Retraction (Standing)
exercises.description: Standing at the wall: chin tuck pressing against the wall. More active than the supine version.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Progressive Nerve Slider
exercises.description: Arm fully extended to the side, wrist flexion + head tilt simultaneously. Full range of motion.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Isometrics 4 Directions (Full)
exercises.description: Flexion, extension, lateral flexion L/R against hand resistance. Full intensity (60–70% max.).
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Heavy Farmer Walk + Overhead
exercises.description: Combination: 30 sec heavy Farmer Walk, then 5 Overhead Press. Test full nerve stress tolerance.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity

exercises.name: Seated Retraction (Moderate Pressure)
exercises.description: Seated with back against the wall: chin tuck with moderate pressure against the wall. Monitor arm symptoms, stop if they increase.
exercises.phase_goal: Pain relief and nerve decompression

exercises.name: Nerve Slider (Moderate)
exercises.description: Seated: arm to the side at shoulder height, flex/extend the wrist with gentle head tilt. Moderate nerve gliding.
exercises.phase_goal: Progressive nerve mobilization and motor control

exercises.name: Isometrics 3 Directions (Moderate)
exercises.description: Flexion, lateral flexion L/R against moderate hand resistance. Extension only lightly. Monitor arm symptoms.
exercises.phase_goal: Cervical-scapulothoracic strengthening + nerve tensioners

exercises.name: Farmer Walk (Moderate)
exercises.description: Moderate weights (4–8 kg per hand), walk 30 seconds. Build nerve stress tolerance. Pause if arm symptoms arise.
exercises.phase_goal: Full loading, nerve stress tolerance, return to activity
